title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 115 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 575–578 (Night 115, continuing directly from nights-114), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 115 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. His cousin ʿAzīza, her brow cut open by his kick, dresses the wound, makes light of it, and again reads his trouble hopefully. Next morning the woman at the window shows him a mirror put into a bag, her hair let down over her face, a pot of green seedlings and a lamp, and vanishes without a word. ʿAzīza, bandaged and weeping over verses of her own hopeless love, explains the signs: at nightfall, go into the garden behind the lane and wait under the lamp. At dusk she gives him a pellet of musk and a line of verse to recite to his beloved only as he leaves her. He finds the garden open and a pavilion set with silk carpets, wine, fruit and flowers, but no one there. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifteenth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and fifteenth night,
sentences.n: al-khāmisata ʿashara, “fifteenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر beside the feminine night, and it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَلَمَّا رَفَصْتُ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي فِي صَدْرِهَا انْقَلَبَتْ عَلَى طَرَفِ الْإِيوَانِ فَجَاءَ الْوَتَدُ فِي جَبْهَتِهَا فَانْفَتَحَ جَبِينُهَا وَسَالَ دَمُهَا فَسَكَنَتْ وَلَمْ تَنْطِقْ بِحَرْفٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba qāla li-tāji al-mulūki fa-lammā rafaṣtu ibnata ʿammī fī ṣadrihā inqalabat ʿalā ṭarafi al-īwāni fa-jāʾa al-watadu fī jabhatihā fa-infataḥa jabīnuhā wa-sāla damuhā fa-sakanat wa-lam tanṭiq bi-ḥarfin wāḥidin
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth said to Tāj al-Mulūk: So when I kicked the daughter of my uncle in her chest, she toppled over onto the edge of the hall, and the peg came into her forehead, and her brow split open and her blood flowed; and she became still and did not utter a single letter.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man said to Tāj al-Mulūk: When I kicked my cousin in the chest, she fell back against the edge of the hall, and the peg struck her forehead. Her brow split open and the blood ran, but she kept still and did not say a single word.
sentences.n: rafaṣtu, “I kicked”: the edition’s form of rafastu, with ṣ for s, as in the night before. al-īwān: the raised, open-fronted hall of the house, where the family sits. lam tanṭiq bi-ḥarfin, “did not utter a letter”: bi-, “with”, marks what is uttered; the idiom means not a single word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَامَتْ فِى الْحَالِ وَأَحْرَقَتْ حُرَاقًا وَحَشَتْ بِهِ ذَلِكَ الْجُرْحَ وَتَعَصَّبَتْ بِعِصَابَةٍ وَمَسَحَتِ الدَّمَ الَّذِي سَالَ عَلَى الْبِسَاطِ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qāmat fī al-ḥāli wa-aḥraqat ḥurāqan wa-ḥashat bihi dhālika al-jurḥa wa-taʿaṣṣabat bi-ʿiṣābatin wa-masaḥati al-dama alladhī sāla ʿalā al-bisāṭi wa-kāna dhālika shayʾun mā kāna
sentences.l: Then she rose at once, and burned a tinder, and stuffed with it that wound, and bound-herself with a bandage, and wiped the blood that had flowed on the carpet; and it was, that, a thing that had not been.
sentences.i: Then she got up at once, burned some tinder and packed the wound with it, bound her head with a bandage, and wiped up the blood that had run onto the carpet; and it was as though nothing had happened.
sentences.n: ḥurāq, “tinder”: rag or fungus burned to ash, used to stop bleeding. wa-kāna dhālika shayʾun mā kāna, “and it was a thing that had not been”, i.e. as if it had never happened. Classical Arabic would want shayʾan after kāna; the text has shayʾun, and it is vocalised as it stands.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَتَتْنِي وَتَبَسَّمَتْ فِي وَجْهِي وَقَالَتْ لِي بِلِينِ الْكَلَامِ وَاللَّهِ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي مَا قُلْتُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ اسْتِهْزَاءً بِكَ وَلَابِهَا وَلَكِنْ قَدْ كُنْتُ مَشْغُولَةً بِوَجَعِ رَأْسِي وَكَانَ فِي خَاطِرِي أَنْ أُخْرِجَ الدَّمَ وَفِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ قَدْ خَفَّتْ رَأْسِي وَخَفَّتْ جَبْهَتِي فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِمَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِكَ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā atatnī wa-tabassamat fī wajhī wa-qālat lī bi-līni al-kalāmi wa-allāhi yā bna ʿammī mā qultu hādhā al-kalāma istihzāʾan bika wa-lā bihā wa-lākin qad kuntu mashghūlatan bi-wajaʿi raʾsī wa-kāna fī khāṭirī an ukhrija al-dama wa-fī hādhihi al-sāʿati qad khaffat raʾsī wa-khaffat jabhatī fa-akhbirnī bi-mā kāna min amrika fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: Then she came to me and smiled in my face and said to me with softness of speech: By God, O son of my uncle, I did not say this speech in mockery of you, nor of her; but I had been occupied with the ache of my head, and it was in my mind to let out the blood; and in this hour my head has grown light and my forehead has grown light. So tell me of what was of your affair on this day.
sentences.i: Then she came to me, smiled at me and said gently, “By God, cousin, I did not say that to mock you, or her. My head had been aching, and I had it in mind to have some blood let; and now my head feels light, and my forehead too. So tell me what happened to you today.”
sentences.n: She turns the wound into a kindness: the kick has done for her what a bloodletting would, she says. ukhrija al-dama, “let out the blood”, is the cure of the day for headache. khaffat raʾsī, “my head has grown light”: the text treats raʾs, “head”, as feminine, as everyday speech often did; Classical has it masculine. wa-lābihā, “nor her”, is printed as one word. bi-līni al-kalāmi: bi-, “with”, of manner, “gently”.

sentences.t: فَحَكَيْتُ لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لِي مِنْهَا فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَبَعْدَ كَلَامِي بَكَيْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakaytu lahā jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lī minhā fī dhālika al-yawmi wa-baʿda kalāmī bakaytu
sentences.l: So I told her all that befell me from her on that day, and after my speech I wept.
sentences.i: So I told her everything that had passed between the lady and me that day, and when I had finished, I wept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي أَبْشِرْ بِنَجَاحِ قَصْدِكَ وَبُلُوغِ أَمَلِكَ إِنَّ هَذِهِ عَلَامَةُ الْقَبُولِ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهَا غَابَتْ عَنْكَ لِأَنَّهَا تُرِيدُأَنْ تَخْتَبِرَكَ وَتَعْرِفَ هَلْ أَنْتَ صَابِرٌ أَوْلَا وَهَلْ أَنْتَ صَادِقٌ فِي مَحَبَّتِهَا أَوْلَا وَفِي غَدٍ تَوَجَّهْ إِلَيْهَا فِي مَكَانِكَ الْأَوَّلِ وَانْظُرْ مَاذَا تُشِيرُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ فَقَدْ قَرُبَتْ أَفْرَاحُكَ وَزَالَتْ أَحْزَانُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā bna ʿammī abshir bi-najāḥi qaṣdika wa-bulūghi amalika inna hādhihi ʿalāmatu al-qabūli wa-dhālika annahā ghābat ʿanka li-annahā turīdu an takhtabiraka wa-taʿrifa hal anta ṣābirun aw lā wa-hal anta ṣādiqun fī maḥabbatihā aw lā wa-fī ghadin tawajjah ilayhā fī makānika al-awwali wa-unẓur mādhā tushīru bihi ilayka fa-qad qarubat afrāḥuka wa-zālat aḥzānuka
sentences.l: And she said: O son of my uncle, rejoice at the success of your aim and the reaching of your hope! This is the sign of acceptance; and that is, she vanished from you because she wants to test you and know whether you are patient or not, and whether you are true in loving her or not. And tomorrow, go to her in your first place and see what she signs to you with; for your joys have drawn near and your griefs have gone.
sentences.i: She said, “Cousin, take heart: you will gain what you seek and reach what you hope for. This is the sign that she accepts you. She vanished from you because she wants to test you, to find out whether you are patient, and whether your love for her is true. Tomorrow go back to her, to the same place as before, and see what sign she makes you. Your joys are near, and your sorrows are over.”
sentences.n: The print has فقل, a misprint for فقد, corrected here: fa-qad qarubat afrāḥuka, “for your joys have drawn near”. turīdu an, “she wants to”, and aw lā, “or not”, are each printed as one word (تريدان, اولا). abshir bi-: the verb takes bi- for the good news received, “rejoice at”. tushīru bihi ilayka: bi-, “with”, marks the sign made; ilayka, “to you”.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ تُسَلِّينِي عَلَى مَابِي وَأَنَا لَمْ أَزَلْ مُتَزَايِدَ الْهُمُومِ وَالْغُمُومِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat tusallīnī ʿalā mā bī wa-anā lam azal mutazāyida al-humūmi wa-al-ghumūmi
sentences.l: And she began to console me over what was in me, and I did not cease being increasing of cares and sorrows.
sentences.i: She went on comforting me in my trouble, but my cares and sorrows only grew.
sentences.n: ʿalā mā bī, “over what is in me”, i.e. my condition; printed as one word, مابي. mutazāyida al-humūmi, “increasing in cares”: a participle with the thing it is increasing in as its genitive. al-humūm wa-al-ghumūm, “cares and sorrows”, is a rhyming pair the Nights loves.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَدَّمَتْ لِيَ الطَّعَامَ فَرَفَصْتُهُ بِرِجْلِي فَانْكَبَّتْ كُلُّ زُبْدِيَّةٍ فِي نَاحِيَةٍ وَقُلْتُ كُلُّ مَنْ كَانَ عَاشِقًا فَهُوَ مَجْنُونٌ لَا يَمِيلُ إِلَى طَعَامٍ وَلَا يَلْتَذُّ بِمَنَامٍ
sentences.tr: thumma qaddamat liya al-ṭaʿāma fa-rafaṣtuhu bi-rijlī fa-inkabbat kullu zubdiyyatin fī nāḥiyatin wa-qultu kullu man kāna ʿāshiqan fa-huwa majnūnun lā yamīlu ilā ṭaʿāmin wa-lā yaltadhdhu bi-manāmin
sentences.l: Then she set before me the food, and I kicked it with my foot, and every bowl was overturned in a direction; and I said: Everyone who is a lover, he is mad: he inclines not to food, nor takes pleasure in sleep.
sentences.i: Then she set food before me, and I kicked it away, and the bowls went flying in every direction. I said, “Whoever is in love is mad: he has no taste for food and no pleasure in sleep.”
sentences.n: zubdiyya: a glazed earthenware bowl of the Egyptian kitchen. ṭaʿām / manām: the saying ends in rhyme. yaltadhdhu bi-: the verb takes bi- for what one enjoys.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي ابْنَةُ عَمِّي عَزِيزَةُ وَاللَّهِ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي إِنَّ هَذِهِ عَلَامَاتُ الْمَحَبَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī ibnatu ʿammī ʿazīzatu wa-allāhi yā bna ʿammī inna hādhihi ʿalāmātu al-maḥabbati
sentences.l: And the daughter of my uncle, ʿAzīza, said to me: By God, O son of my uncle, these are the signs of love.
sentences.i: My cousin ʿAzīza said to me, “By God, cousin, these are the signs of love.”

sentences.t: وَسَالَتْ دُمُوعُهَا وَلَمَّتْ شَقَافَةَ الزَّبَادِي وَمَسَحَتِ الطَّعَامَ وَجَلَسَتْ تُسَامِرُنِي وَأَنَا أَدْعُواللَّهَ أَنْ يُصْبِحَ الصَّبَاحُ
sentences.tr: wa-sālat dumūʿuhā wa-lammat shaqāfata al-zabādī wa-masaḥati al-ṭaʿāma wa-jalasat tusāmirunī wa-anā adʿū allāha an yuṣbiḥa al-ṣabāḥu
sentences.l: And her tears flowed, and she gathered the shards of the bowls and wiped up the food, and sat keeping-me-company-in-talk, while I was praying God that the morning would dawn.
sentences.i: Her tears ran down; she gathered up the broken pieces of the bowls, wiped up the food, and sat talking with me through the night, while I prayed God for the morning to come.
sentences.n: shaqāfa, “shards”: the colloquial word for broken pottery. tusāmirunī: she sits up with me in night-time talk (samar). adʿū allāha, “I pray God”, is printed as one word, ادعوالله.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَضَاءَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ تَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَيْهَا وَدَخَلْتُ ذَلِكَ الزُّقَاقَ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَجَلَسْتُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْمَسْطَبَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-aḍāʾa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa tawajjahtu ilayhā wa-dakhaltu dhālika al-zuqāqa bi-surʿatin wa-jalastu ʿalā tilka al-masṭabati
sentences.l: And when the morning dawned and shone with its light and gleamed, I went to her and entered that lane in haste and sat on that bench.
sentences.i: When morning came, shining with its light, I went to her. I hurried into the lane and sat down on the same bench.
sentences.n: al-ṣabāḥ … lāḥa: the dawn formula rhymes (ṣabāḥ / lāḥ). masṭaba (so spelled here, often maṣṭaba): the stone bench built against the front of a house or shop. bi-nūrihi: bi-, “with”, its light.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالطَّاقَةِ قَدِ انْفَتَحَتْ وَأَبْرَزَتْ رَأْسَهَا مِنْهَا وَهِيَ تَضْحَكُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ṭāqati qadi infataḥat wa-abrazat raʾsahā minhā wa-hiya taḍḥaku
sentences.l: And behold, the window had opened, and she put out her head from it, and she was laughing.
sentences.i: And there was the window, opening; she put her head out of it, laughing.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-al-ṭāqati: after idhā of surprise, bi- only marks what appears: “and behold, the window”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَابَتْ وَرَجَعَتْ وَمَعَهَا مِرْآةٌ وَكِيسٌ وَقَصْرِيَّةٌ مُمْتَلِئَةٌ بِزَرْعٍ أَخْضَرَ وَفِي يَدِهَا قِنْدِيلٌ
sentences.tr: thumma ghābat wa-rajaʿat wa-maʿahā mirʾātun wa-kīsun wa-qaṣriyyatun mumtaliʾatun bi-zarʿin akhḍara wa-fī yadihā qindīlun
sentences.l: Then she vanished, and returned, and with her a mirror and a bag and a pot full of green growth, and in her hand a lamp.
sentences.i: Then she disappeared, and came back with a mirror, a bag, and a pot full of green seedlings, and a lamp in her hand.
sentences.n: qaṣriyya: an earthenware pot, here one planted with young green shoots. bi-zarʿin: the participle mumtaliʾa, “filled”, takes bi- for what fills it.

sentences.t: فَأَوَّلُ مَا فَعَلَتْ أَخَذَتِ الْمِرْآةَ فِي يَدِهَا وَأَدْخَلَتْهَا فِى الْكِيسِ ثُمَّ رَبَطَتْهُ وَرَمَتْهُ فِى الْبَيْتِ ثُمَّ أَرْخَتْ شَعْرَهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا ثُمَّ وَضَعَتِ الْقِنْدِيلَ عَلَى رَأْسِ الزَّرْعِ لَحْظَةً ثُمَّ أَخَذَتْ جَمِيعَ ذَلِكَ وَانْصَرَفَتْ بِهِ وَأَغْلَقَتِ الطَّاقَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-awwalu mā faʿalat akhadhati al-mirʾāta fī yadihā wa-adkhalathā fī al-kīsi thumma rabaṭathu wa-ramathu fī al-bayti thumma arkhat shaʿrahā ʿalā wajhihā thumma waḍaʿati al-qindīla ʿalā raʾsi al-zarʿi laḥẓatan thumma akhadhat jamīʿa dhālika wa-inṣarafat bihi wa-aghlaqati al-ṭāqata
sentences.l: And the first of what she did: she took the mirror in her hand and put it into the bag, then tied it and threw it into the house; then she let down her hair over her face; then she set the lamp on the top of the growth a moment; then she took all of that and went away with it and shut the window.
sentences.i: The first thing she did was to take the mirror and put it into the bag; then she tied the bag and threw it back into the room. Then she let her hair fall over her face. Then she held the lamp over the top of the seedlings for a moment. Then she took it all, went away with it, and shut the window.
sentences.n: inṣarafat bihi: bi-, “with”, she went off taking it with her.

sentences.t: فَانْفَطَرَ قَلْبِي مِنْ هَذَا الْحَالِ وَمِنْ إِشَارَاتِهَا الْخَفِيَّةِ وَرُمُوزِهَا الْمَخْفِيَّةِ وَهِيَ لَمْ تُكَلِّمْنِي بِكَلِمَةٍ قَطُّ فَاشْتَدَّ لِذَلِكَ غَرَامِي وَزَادَ وَجْدِي وَهُيَامِى
sentences.tr: fa-infaṭara qalbī min hādhā al-ḥāli wa-min ishārātihā al-khafiyyati wa-rumūzihā al-makhfiyyati wa-hiya lam tukallimnī bi-kalimatin qaṭṭu fa-ishtadda li-dhālika gharāmī wa-zāda wajdī wa-huyāmī
sentences.l: And my heart split from this state and from her hidden signs and her concealed riddles, while she had not spoken to me a word ever; and for that my passion grew fierce and my longing and my love-madness increased.
sentences.i: My heart broke at all this, at her secret signs and hidden riddles, when she had never once spoken a word to me; and it made my passion fiercer, my longing and my madness greater.
sentences.n: al-khafiyya / al-makhfiyya, “hidden / concealed”: a rhyming pair. li-dhālika: li-, “for”, of cause, “because of that”. huyām: the lover’s wandering madness, from hāma, “to wander distraught”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي رَجَعْتُ عَلَى عَقِبِي وَأَنَا بَاكِى الْعَيْنِ حَزِينُ الْقَلْبِ حَتَّى دَخَلْتُ الْبَيْتَ فَرَأَيْتُ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي قَاعِدَةً وَوَجْهُهَا إِلَى الْحَائِطِ
sentences.tr: thumma innī rajaʿtu ʿalā ʿaqibī wa-anā bākī al-ʿayni ḥazīnu al-qalbi ḥattā dakhaltu al-bayta fa-raʾaytu ibnata ʿammī qāʿidatan wa-wajhuhā ilā al-ḥāʾiṭi
sentences.l: Then I turned back on my heel, weeping of eye, grieved of heart, until I entered the house, and I saw the daughter of my uncle sitting with her face to the wall.
sentences.i: Then I turned back, weeping and heavy-hearted, until I came into the house; and there was my cousin, sitting with her face to the wall.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ احْتَرَقَ قَلْبُهَا مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْغَمِّ وَالْغَيْرَةِ وَلَكِنَّ مَحَبَّتَهَا مَنَعَتْهَا أَنْ تُخْبِرَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مِمَّا عِنْدَهَا مِنَ الْغَرَامِ لَمَّا رَأَتْ مَا أَنَا فِيهِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْوَجْدِ وَالْهُيَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi iḥtaraqa qalbuhā mina al-hammi wa-al-ghammi wa-al-ghayrati wa-lākinna maḥabbatahā manaʿathā an tukhbiranī bi-shayʾin mimmā ʿindahā mina al-gharāmi lammā raʾat mā anā fīhi min kathrati al-wajdi wa-al-huyāmi
sentences.l: And her heart had burned from care and grief and jealousy; but her love prevented her from telling me anything of what was with her of passion, when she saw what I was in of the abundance of longing and love-madness.
sentences.i: Her heart was burning with care, grief and jealousy; but her love kept her from telling me anything of her own passion, when she saw how deep I was in longing and madness.
sentences.n: tukhbiranī bi-shayʾin: the verb akhbara takes bi- for the thing told.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهَا فَرَأَيْتُ عَلَى رَأْسِهَا عِصَابَتَيْنِ إِحْدٰهُمَا مِنَ الْوَقْعَةِ عَلَى جَبْهَتِهَا وَالْأُخْرَى عَلَى عَيْنِهَا بِسَبَبِ وَجَعٍ أَصَابَهَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ بُكَائِهَا وَهِيَ فِي أَسْوَءِ الْحَالَاتِ تَبْكِي وَتُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓartu ilayhā fa-raʾaytu ʿalā raʾsihā ʿiṣābatayni iḥdāhumā mina al-waqʿati ʿalā jabhatihā wa-al-ukhrā ʿalā ʿaynihā bi-sababi wajaʿin aṣābahā min shiddati bukāʾihā wa-hiya fī aswaʾi al-ḥālāti tabkī wa-tunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then I looked at her and saw on her head two bandages, one of them from the fall, on her forehead, and the other on her eye, because of a pain that struck her from the vehemence of her weeping; and she was in the worst of states, weeping and reciting these verses:
sentences.i: Then I looked at her and saw two bandages on her head: one over her forehead, from the fall, and the other over her eye, which ached from all her weeping. She was in the worst of states, weeping, and reciting these verses:
sentences.n: iḥdāhumā, “one of them”: the print writes the long ā with a small upright alif. aswaʾ, “worst”: the print spells it اسوء, for أسوأ, with the hamza on the line.

sentences.t:
اَعُدُّ اللَّيَالِيْ لَيْلَةً بَعْدَ لَيْلَةٍ * وَقَدْ عِشْتُ دَهْرًا لَا اَعُدُّ اللَّيَالِيَا
خَلِيلَيَّ وَاللّٰهِ لَا اَمْلِكُ الَّذِيْ * قَضَى اللّٰهُ فِيْ لَيْلَى وَلَا مَا قَضَى لِيَا
قَضَاهَا لِغَيْرِيْ وَابْتَلَانِيْ بِحُبِّهَا * فَهَلَّا بِشَيْءٍ غَيْرَ لَيْلَى ابْتَلَانِيَا
sentences.tr:
aʿuddu al-layālī laylatan baʿda laylatin * wa-qad ʿishtu dahran lā aʿuddu al-layāliyā
khalīlayya wa-allāhi lā amliku alladhī * qaḍā allāhu fī laylā wa-lā mā qaḍā liyā
qaḍāhā li-ghayrī wa-ibtalānī bi-ḥubbihā * fa-hallā bi-shayʾin ghayra laylā ibtalāniyā
sentences.l:
I count the nights, night after night, * and I had lived an age not counting the nights.
My two friends, by God, I have no power over what * God decreed concerning Laylā, nor over what He decreed for me.
He decreed her for another, and tried me with love of her: * then why not with something other than Laylā did He try me?
sentences.i:
I count the nights, one night and then another, * I who once lived for years and never counted nights.
My friends, by God, I have no power over what * God has decreed for Laylā, nor what He decreed for me.
He gave her to another, and made me suffer love of her: * why could He not have tried me with anything but Laylā?
sentences.n: Lines from the poetry of love for Laylā that tradition gives to Majnūn, “the madman”, Qays ibn al-Mulawwaḥ. ʿAzīza sings them of herself: the man she loves is given to another. The long -ā at the end of each line (al-layāliyā, liyā, ibtalāniyā) is the rhyme’s lengthening of the final vowel. ibtalānī bi-: “He tried me with”, bi- marking the affliction.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا نَظَرَتْ إِلَيَّ فَرَأَتْنِي وَهِيَ تَبْكِي فَمَسَحَتْ دُمُوعَهَا وَنَهَضَتْ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ تَقْدِرْ أَنْ تَتَكَلَّمَ مِمَّاهِيَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْوَجْدِ وَلَمْ تَزَلْ سَاكِتَةً بُرْهَةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā naẓarat ilayya fa-raʾatnī wa-hiya tabkī fa-masaḥat dumūʿahā wa-nahaḍat ilayya wa-lam taqdir an tatakallama mimmā hiya fīhi mina al-wajdi wa-lam tazal sākitatan burhatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: And when she had finished her poetry, she looked at me and saw me, weeping as she was; and she wiped her tears and rose to me, and could not speak from what she was in of longing; and she did not cease being silent a while of time.
sentences.i: When she had finished her poem she looked up and saw me, still weeping herself. She wiped away her tears and rose to meet me, but she could not speak, so deep was her longing, and for a while she stayed silent.
sentences.n: mimmā hiya fīhi, “from what she was in”, is printed as one word, مماهي.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ يَابْنَ عَمِّي أَخْبِرْنِي بِمَا حَصَلَ لَكَ مِنْهَا فِي هَذِهِ الْمَرَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika qālat yā bna ʿammī akhbirnī bi-mā ḥaṣala laka minhā fī hādhihi al-marrati
sentences.l: Then after that she said: O son of my uncle, tell me of what came to you from her this time.
sentences.i: After that she said, “Cousin, tell me what passed between you and her this time.”
sentences.n: yā bna, “O son”, is printed as one word, يابن.

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرْتُهَا بِجَمِيعِ مَاحَصَلَ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhbartuhā bi-jamīʿi mā ḥaṣala lī
sentences.l: So I told her of all that came to me.
sentences.i: So I told her everything that had happened.
sentences.n: mā ḥaṣala, “what happened”, is printed as one word, ماحصل.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِيَ اصْبِرْ فَقَدْ آنَ أَوَانُ وِصَالِكَ وَظَفِرْتَ بِبُلُوغِ آمَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat liya iṣbir fa-qad āna awānu wiṣālika wa-ẓafirta bi-bulūghi āmālika
sentences.l: And she said to me: Be patient, for the time of your union has come, and you have won the reaching of your hopes.
sentences.i: She said to me, “Be patient: the time for you to be united with her has come, and you have won what you hoped for.”
sentences.n: wiṣālika / āmālika: rhymed prose. ẓafirta bi-, “you have won”: the verb takes bi- for the prize.

sentences.t: أَمَّا إِشَارَتُهَا لَكَ بِالْمِرْآةِ وَكَوْنُهَا أَدْخَلَتْهَا فِى الْكِيسِ فَإِنَّهَا تَقُولُ لَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَغْطِسَ الشَّمْسُ
sentences.tr: ammā ishāratuhā laka bi-al-mirʾāti wa-kawnuhā adkhalathā fī al-kīsi fa-innahā taqūlu laka ilā an taghṭisa al-shamsu
sentences.l: As for her signing to you with the mirror, and her having put it into the bag: she is saying to you, until the sun plunges down.
sentences.i: “Her sign with the mirror, when she put it into the bag, tells you: wait until the sun has sunk.
sentences.n: The mirror is the sun, and the bag it disappears into is the sunset. taghṭisa, “plunges”, is the everyday word for diving or sinking under water. ishāratuhā laka bi-: “her signing to you with”, bi- marking the thing she signs with.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا إِرْخَاؤُهَا شَعْرَهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا فَإِنَّهَا تَقُولُ لَكَ إِذَا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ وَانْسَدَلَ سَوَادُ الظَّلَامِ وَعَلَا نُورَ النَّهَارِ فَتَعَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā irkhāʾuhā shaʿrahā ʿalā wajhihā fa-innahā taqūlu laka idhā aqbala al-laylu wa-insadala sawādu al-ẓalāmi wa-ʿalā nūra al-nahāri fa-taʿāla
sentences.l: And as for her letting down her hair over her face: she is saying to you, when the night comes on and the blackness of the dark is let down and rises over the light of day, then come.
sentences.i: Her letting her hair fall over her face tells you: when night comes on, and the black of darkness falls like a veil and covers the light of day, then come.
sentences.n: wa-ʿalā nūra al-nahāri, “and rises over the light of day”: read here with the darkness as subject and the light as object, ʿalā meaning to rise above and cover. The hair let down is the night let down (insadala, “hung down like a curtain”).

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا إِشَارَتُهَا لَكَ بِالْقَصْرِيَّةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الزَّرْعُ فَإِنَّهَا تَقُولُ لَكَ إِذَا جِئْتَ فَادْخُلِ الْبُسْتَانَ الَّذِى وَرَاءَ الزُّقَاقِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā ishāratuhā laka bi-al-qaṣriyyati allatī fīhā al-zarʿu fa-innahā taqūlu laka idhā jiʾta fa-udkhuli al-bustāna alladhī warāʾa al-zuqāqi
sentences.l: And as for her signing to you with the pot in which is the growth: she is saying to you, when you come, enter the garden that is behind the lane.
sentences.i: Her sign with the pot of seedlings tells you: when you come, go into the garden behind the lane.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا إِشَارَتُهَا لَكَ بِالْقِنْدِيلِ فَإِنَّهَا تَقُولُ لَكَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْبُسْتَانَ فَامْشِ فِيهِ وَأَيَّ مَوْضِعٍ وَجَدْتَ فِيهِ الْقِنْدِيلَ مُضِيأً فَتَوَجَّهْ إِلَيْهِ وَاجْلِسْ تَحْتَهُ وَانْتَظِرْنِي فَإِنَّ هَوَاكَ قَاتِلِي
sentences.tr: wa-ammā ishāratuhā laka bi-al-qindīli fa-innahā taqūlu laka idhā dakhalta al-bustāna fa-imshi fīhi wa-ayya mawḍiʿin wajadta fīhi al-qindīla muḍīʾan fa-tawajjah ilayhi wa-ijlis taḥtahu wa-intaẓirnī fa-inna hawāka qātilī
sentences.l: And as for her signing to you with the lamp: she is saying to you, when you have entered the garden, walk in it, and whatever place you find the lamp shining in, go to it and sit beneath it and wait for me; for love of you is my killer.
sentences.i: And her sign with the lamp tells you: when you are in the garden, walk through it, and wherever you find the lamp alight, go to it, sit beneath it and wait for me; for my love for you is killing me.”
sentences.n: muḍīʾan, “shining”: the print spells it مضيأ, for مضيئا, with the hamza on an alif. fa-inna hawāka qātilī, “for love of you is killing me”: ʿAzīza speaks the lady’s message in the lady’s voice; the words are hers too.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَ ابْنَةِ عَمِّي صِحْتُ مِنْ فَرْطِ الْغَرَامِ وَقُلْتُ كَمْ تَعِدِينِى وَأَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْهَا وَلَا أَحْصُلُ مَقْصُودِي وَلَا أَجِدُ لِتَفْسِيرِكِ مَعْنًى صَحِيحًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāma ibnati ʿammī ṣiḥtu min farṭi al-gharāmi wa-qultu kam taʿidīnī wa-atawajjahu ilayhā wa-lā aḥṣulu maqṣūdī wa-lā ajidu li-tafsīriki maʿnan ṣaḥīḥan
sentences.l: And when I heard the speech of the daughter of my uncle, I cried out from excess of passion and said: How often you promise me, and I go to her and do not obtain my aim, and do not find for your interpreting a true meaning!
sentences.i: When I heard what my cousin said, I cried out in the excess of my passion: “How often you make me promises, and I go to her and do not get what I want! I find no true meaning in your readings.”
sentences.n: aḥṣulu maqṣūdī, “obtain my aim”: ḥaṣala here takes a direct object, as in everyday speech; Classical says ḥaṣala ʿalā. li-tafsīriki: li-, “for”, “find for your interpretation a meaning”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ ضَحِكَتْ بِنْتُ عَمِّي وَقَالَتْ لِي بَقِيَ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الصَّبْرِ أَنْ تَصْبِرَ بَقِيَّةَ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ إِلَى أَنْ يُوَلِّىَ النَّهَارُ وَيُقْبِلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ فَتَحْظَى بِالْوِصَالِ وَبُلُوغِ الْآمَالِ وَهَذَا الْكَلَامُ صِدْقٌ بِغَيْرِ مَيْنٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ḍaḥikat bintu ʿammī wa-qālat lī baqiya ʿalayka mina al-ṣabri an taṣbira baqiyyata hādhā al-yawmi ilā an yuwalliya al-nahāru wa-yuqbila al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri fa-taḥẓā bi-al-wiṣāli wa-bulūghi al-āmāli wa-hādhā al-kalāmu ṣidqun bi-ghayri maynin
sentences.l: And at that the daughter of my uncle laughed and said to me: There remains upon you of patience that you be patient the rest of this day, until the day turns away and the night comes on with its thick-darkness; then you will win union and the reaching of hopes. And this speech is truth without falsehood.
sentences.i: At that my cousin laughed and said to me, “All the patience left for you is to wait out the rest of today, until the day is gone and the night comes on in its darkness; then you will have your union and all you hoped for. This is the truth, and no lie.”
sentences.n: nahār / iʿtikār, wiṣāl / āmāl: two rhymed pairs. iʿtikār: the thickening of the dark. mayn, “falsehood”: a rare word, met mostly in the set phrase ṣidqun bi-ghayri maynin, “truth without lie”. bi-al-iʿtikāri: bi-, “with”, what the night brings; fa-taḥẓā bi-: the verb takes bi- for what is won.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: Then she recited these two lines:
sentences.i: Then she recited these two lines:

sentences.t:
دَرِّجِ الْاَيَّامَ تَنْدَرِجْ * وَبُيُوْتُ الْهَمِّ لَا تَلِجْ
رُبَّ اَمْرٍ عَزَّ مَطْلَبُهُ * قَرَّبَتْهُ سَاعَةُ الْفَرَجْ
sentences.tr:
darriji al-ayyāma tandarij * wa-buyūtu al-hammi lā talij
rubba amrin ʿazza maṭlabuhu * qarrabathu sāʿatu al-faraj
sentences.l:
Let the days roll on, they will roll on, * and the houses of care do not enter.
Many a matter whose seeking was hard * the hour of relief brought near.
sentences.i:
Let the days roll by, and by they roll; * and do not go into the houses of care.
How often a thing too hard to reach * is brought close by the hour of release.
sentences.n: wa-buyūtu al-hammi lā talij, “and the houses of care, do not enter”: the print points buyūtu as a subject put first, “as for the houses of care, do not go in”. rubba, “many a”: it takes an indefinite noun in the genitive (amrin). al-faraj: release from distress, relief that comes from God.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَصَارَتْ تُسَلِّينِى بِلِينِ الْكَلَامِ وَلَمْ تَجْسُرْ أَنْ تَأْتِيَنِى بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ مَخَافَةً مِنْ غَضَبِي عَلَيْهَا وَرَجَاءَ مَيْلِي إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā aqbalat ʿalayya wa-ṣārat tusallīnī bi-līni al-kalāmi wa-lam tajsur an taʾtiyanī bi-shayʾin mina al-ṭaʿāmi makhāfatan min ghaḍabī ʿalayhā wa-rajāʾa maylī ilayhā
sentences.l: Then she turned to me and began to console me with softness of speech, and did not dare to bring me anything of food, in fear of my anger at her and in hope of my inclining to her.
sentences.i: Then she turned to me and began to comfort me with gentle words. She did not dare bring me any food, for fear of my anger, and in the hope that I might warm to her.
sentences.n: taʾtiyanī bi-shayʾin: atā bi-, “to come with”, is “to bring”.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا قَصْدٌ إِلَّا أَنَّهَا أَتَتْ إِلَيَّ وَقَلَعَتْنِي ثِيَابِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam yakun lahā qaṣdun illā annahā atat ilayya wa-qalaʿatnī thiyābī
sentences.l: And she had no aim but that she came to me and took-off-me my clothes.
sentences.i: All she did was to come to me and take off my clothes.
sentences.n: The print has انت, a misprint for اتت, corrected here: atat, “she came”. qalaʿatnī thiyābī, “she took me off my clothes”: qalaʿa, “to pull off”, with two objects, the person and the clothes, as in everyday speech.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي اقْعُدْ حَتَّى أُحَدِّثَكَ بِمَا يُسَلِّيكَ إِلَى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ وَإِنْ شَاءَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى مَايَأْتِي اللَّيْلُ إِلَّا وَأَنْتَ عِنْدَ مَحْبُوبَتِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat yā bna ʿammī uqʿud ḥattā uḥaddithaka bi-mā yusallīka ilā ākhiri al-nahāri wa-in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā mā yaʾtī al-laylu illā wa-anta ʿinda maḥbūbatika
sentences.l: Then she said: O son of my uncle, sit, so that I may tell you of what will console you until the end of the day; and if God, exalted is He, wills, the night will not come but that you are with your beloved.
sentences.i: Then she said, “Cousin, sit down, and I will tell you stories to pass the time until the end of the day; and, God willing, night will not fall before you are with your beloved.”
sentences.n: shāʾa allāhu and mā yaʾtī are each printed as one word (شاءالله, مايأتي). mā … illā wa-: “the night does not come except that you are …”, i.e. by nightfall you will be there. uḥaddithaka bi-: the verb takes bi- for what is told.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَلْتَفِتْ إِلَيْهَا وَصِرْتُ أَنْتَظِرُ مَجِيءَ اللَّيْلِ وَأَقُولُ يَارَبِّ عَجِّلْ بِمَجِيءِ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam altafit ilayhā wa-ṣirtu antaẓiru majīʾa al-layli wa-aqūlu yā rabbi ʿajjil bi-majīʾi al-layli
sentences.l: But I paid no heed to her, and I began waiting for the coming of the night, and saying: O Lord, hasten the coming of the night!
sentences.i: But I paid her no attention. I sat waiting for night to come, saying, “O Lord, bring the night quickly!”
sentences.n: yā rabbi, “O Lord”, is printed as one word, يارب. ʿajjil bi-: “hasten”, the verb taking bi- for what is hurried on.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَتَى اللَّيْلُ بَكَتِ ابْنَةُ عَمِّي بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَأَعْطَتْنِي حَبَّةَ مِسْكٍ خَالِصٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā atā al-laylu bakati ibnatu ʿammī bukāʾan shadīdan wa-aʿṭatnī ḥabbata miskin khāliṣin
sentences.l: And when the night came, the daughter of my uncle wept a vehement weeping and gave me a grain of pure musk.
sentences.i: When night came, my cousin wept bitterly, and gave me a pellet of pure musk.
sentences.n: The print has بكاوشديدا, a misprint for بكاء شديدا, corrected here: bukāʾan shadīdan, “a vehement weeping”, the verb’s own noun used to say how she wept.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي اجْعَلْ هَذِهِ الْحَبَّةَ فِي فَمِكَ فَإِذَا اجْتَمَعْتَ بِمَحْبُوبَتِكَ وَقَضَيْتَ مِنْهَا حَاجَتَكَ وَسَمَحَتْ لَكَ بِمَا تَمَنَّيْتَ فَأَنْشِدْهَا هَذَا الْبَيْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā bna ʿammī ijʿal hādhihi al-ḥabbata fī famika fa-idhā ijtamaʿta bi-maḥbūbatika wa-qaḍayta minhā ḥājataka wa-samaḥat laka bi-mā tamannayta fa-anshidhā hādhā al-bayta
sentences.l: And she said: O son of my uncle, put this grain in your mouth; and when you have met with your beloved and fulfilled your need of her, and she has granted you what you wished, then recite to her this line:
sentences.i: She said, “Cousin, put this pellet in your mouth; and when you are with your beloved, and have had your desire of her, and she has granted you all you wished, recite this line to her:
sentences.n: ijtamaʿta bi-, “you met with”: the verb takes bi- for the one met. qaḍayta minhā ḥājataka, “fulfilled your need of her”, is the usual plain phrase for lovemaking. samaḥat laka bi-: “granted you”, bi- marking what is granted.

sentences.t: اَلَا اَيُّهَا الْعُشَّاقُ بِاللّٰهِ خَبِّرُوْا * اِذَا اشْتَدَّ عِشْقٌ بِالْفَتَى كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ
sentences.tr: alā ayyuhā al-ʿushshāqu bi-allāhi khabbirū * idhā ishtadda ʿishqun bi-al-fatā kayfa yaṣnaʿu
sentences.l: Ho, O you lovers, by God, tell: * when passion grows fierce in the young man, what does he do?
sentences.i: You lovers, tell me, in God’s name: * when love grows fierce in a young man, what is he to do?”
sentences.n: bi-allāhi: bi- of the oath, “by God”. bi-al-fatā: bi-, “in”, the passion takes hold in the young man.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَبَّلَتْنِي وَحَلَّفَتْنِي أَنِّي لَاأُنْشِدُهَا ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتَ الشِّعْرَ إِلَّا وَقْتَ خُرُوجِي مِنْ عِنْدِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qabbalatnī wa-ḥallafatnī annī lā unshiduhā dhālika al-bayta al-shiʿra illā waqta khurūjī min ʿindihā
sentences.l: Then she kissed me and made me swear that I would not recite to her that line, the poetry, except at the time of my going out from her.
sentences.i: Then she kissed me and made me swear not to recite that line to her until I was leaving her.
sentences.n: lā unshiduhā, “I will not recite to her”, is printed as one word, لاانشدها. al-bayta al-shiʿra, “the line, the verse”: two nouns set side by side, as in everyday speech, for “that line of verse”.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qultu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And I said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: And I said, “Hearing and obedience.”
sentences.n: samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan: two accusatives with an understood verb, “(I give) hearing and obedience”, the set reply of a willing promise.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ وَقْتَ الْعِشَاءِ وَمَشَيْتُ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ مَاشِيًا حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ فَوَجَدْتُ بَابَهُ مَفْتُوحًا فَدَخَلْتُهُ فَرَأَيْتُ نُورًا عَلَى بُعْدٍ فَقَصَدْتُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajtu waqta al-ʿishāʾi wa-mashaytu wa-lam azal māshiyan ḥattā waṣaltu ilā al-bustāni fa-wajadtu bābahu maftūḥan fa-dakhaltuhu fa-raʾaytu nūran ʿalā buʿdin fa-qaṣadtuhu
sentences.l: Then I went out at the time of the evening prayer, and walked, and did not cease walking until I reached the garden, and found its gate open; so I entered it, and saw a light at a distance, and made for it.
sentences.i: Then I went out at the hour of the evening prayer and walked, and kept on walking until I came to the garden. I found its gate open and went in, and I saw a light in the distance, and made my way towards it.
sentences.n: waqt al-ʿishāʾ: the time of the last prayer of the day, after nightfall.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَجَدْتُ مَقْعَدًا عَظِيمًا مَعْقُودًا عَلَيْهِ قُبَّةٌ مِنَ الْعَاجِ وَالْآبَنُوسِ وَالْقِنْدِيلُ مُعَلَّقٌ فِي وَسَطِ تِلْكَ الْقُبَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣaltu ilayhi wajadtu maqʿadan ʿaẓīman maʿqūdan ʿalayhi qubbatun mina al-ʿāji wa-al-ābanūsi wa-al-qindīlu muʿallaqun fī wasaṭi tilka al-qubbati
sentences.l: And when I reached it, I found a great sitting-place, vaulted over it a dome of ivory and ebony, and the lamp hanging in the middle of that dome.
sentences.i: When I reached it, I found a great open pavilion, roofed with a dome of ivory and ebony, and the lamp hanging in the middle of the dome.
sentences.n: maqʿad: a raised, open-sided sitting room, here a garden pavilion. maʿqūdan ʿalayhi qubbatun, “vaulted over it a dome”: the participle agrees with the pavilion and takes the dome as its subject.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ الْمَقْعَدُ مَفْرُوشٌ بِالْبُسُطِ الْحَرِيرِ الْمُزَرْكَشَةِ بِالذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَهُنَاكَ شَمْعَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ مَوْقُودَةٌ فِي شَمْعَدَانٍ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ تَحْتَ الْقِنْدِيلِ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika al-maqʿadu mafrūshun bi-al-busuṭi al-ḥarīri al-muzarkashati bi-al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati wa-hunāka shamʿatun kabīratun mawqūdatun fī shamʿadānin mina al-dhahabi taḥta al-qindīli
sentences.l: And that sitting-place was spread with carpets, the silk, embroidered with gold and silver; and there was a great candle lit in a candlestick of gold beneath the lamp.
sentences.i: The pavilion was spread with silk carpets embroidered in gold and silver, and beneath the lamp a great candle burned in a golden candlestick.
sentences.n: al-busuṭ al-ḥarīr, “the carpets, the silk”: a material noun set after its noun like an adjective, as everyday Arabic does. muzarkasha: worked with gold thread (zarkasha). bi-: “with”, what the floor is spread with and what the carpets are worked with.

sentences.t: وَفِي وَسَطِ الْمَقْعَدِ فَسْقِيَّةٌ فِيهَا أَنْوَاعُ التَّصَاوِيرِ وَبِجَانِبِ تِلْكَ الْفَسْقِيَّةِ سُفْرَةٌ مُغَطَّاةٌ بِفُوطَةٍ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ وَإِلَى جَانِبِهَا بَاطِيَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ مِنَ الصِّينِيِّ مَمْلُوءَةٌ خَمْرًا وَفِيهَا قَدَحٌ مِنْ بِلَّوْرٍ مُزَرْكَشٌ بِالذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī wasaṭi al-maqʿadi fasqiyyatun fīhā anwāʿu al-taṣāwīri wa-bi-jānibi tilka al-fasqiyyati sufratun mughaṭṭātun bi-fūṭatin mina al-ḥarīri wa-ilā jānibihā bāṭiyatun kabīratun mina al-ṣīniyyi mamlūʾatun khamran wa-fīhā qadaḥun min billawrin muzarkashun bi-al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And in the middle of the sitting-place a fountain-basin in which were kinds of figures; and beside that basin a table-cloth covered with a napkin of silk; and next to it a great wine-bowl of china filled with wine, and in it a cup of crystal worked with gold.
sentences.i: In the middle of the pavilion was a fountain basin adorned with all kinds of figures; beside the basin a spread of food covered with a silk cloth; and next to that a great china bowl filled with wine, with a crystal cup in it, worked with gold.
sentences.n: fasqiyya: a shallow fountain basin set in the floor. sufra: the leather or cloth on which a meal is laid, and so the meal itself. bāṭiya: a large wide vessel for wine. al-ṣīnī, “the Chinese”, is porcelain. bi-jānibi: bi-, “at”, “beside”.

sentences.t: وَإِلَى جَانِبِ الْجَمِيعِ طَبَقٌ كَبِيرٌ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ مُغَطًّى فَكَشَفْتُهُ فَرَأَيْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ سَائِرِ الْفَوَاكِهِ مَابَيْنَ تِينٍ وَرُمَّانٍ وَعِنَبٍ وَنَارَنْجٍ وَأُتْرُجٍّ وَكَبَّادٍ وَبَيْنَهَا أَنْوَاعُ الرَّيَاحِينِ مِنْ وَرْدٍ وَيَاسَمِينٍ وَآسٍ وَنِسْرِينٍ وَنَرْجِسٍ وَمِنْ سَائِرِ الْمَشْمُومَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-ilā jānibi al-jamīʿi ṭabaqun kabīrun min fiḍḍatin mughaṭṭan fa-kashaftuhu fa-raʾaytu fīhi min sāʾiri al-fawākihi mā bayna tīnin wa-rummānin wa-ʿinabin wa-nāranjin wa-utrujjin wa-kabbādin wa-baynahā anwāʿu al-rayāḥīni min wardin wa-yāsamīnin wa-āsin wa-nisrīnin wa-narjisin wa-min sāʾiri al-mashmūmāti
sentences.l: And beside all of it a great tray of silver, covered; and I uncovered it and saw in it of all the fruits, what is between fig and pomegranate and grape and bitter-orange and citron and kabbād; and among them kinds of sweet-herbs, of rose and jasmine and myrtle and eglantine and narcissus, and of all the things-to-be-smelled.
sentences.i: Beside it all stood a great covered silver tray. I uncovered it, and in it was every kind of fruit: figs and pomegranates, grapes, bitter oranges, citrons and kabbād; and among them all kinds of sweet-smelling flowers, roses, jasmine, myrtle, eglantine and narcissus, and every other fragrant thing.
sentences.n: mā bayna, “what is between”, is printed as one word, مابين, and introduces the list. kabbād: a large sour citrus fruit, a kind of citron. nisrīn: the eglantine or musk rose. al-mashmūmāt: “things to be smelled”, flowers and herbs kept for their scent.

sentences.t: فَهِمْتُ بِذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ وَفَرِحْتُ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ وَزَالَ عَنِّي الْهَمُّ وَالتَّرَحُ
sentences.tr: fa-himtu bi-dhālika al-makāni wa-fariḥtu ghāyata al-faraḥi wa-zāla ʿannī al-hammu wa-al-taraḥu
sentences.l: And I was enraptured with that place, and rejoiced the utmost of rejoicing, and care and sorrow departed from me.
sentences.i: I was entranced by the place and filled with joy, and all my care and sorrow left me.
sentences.n: fa-himtu, “I was enraptured”, from hāma: the print points it, so that it is not read fa-fahimtu, “I understood”. hāma bi-: “to be infatuated with”, the verb choosing bi-. al-faraḥ / al-taraḥ, “joy / sorrow”: a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: لَكِنِّي مَا وَجَدْتُ فِي هَذِهِ الدَّارِ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: lākinnī mā wajadtu fī hādhihi al-dāri aḥadan min khalqi allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: But I did not find in this dwelling anyone of the creatures of God, exalted is He.
sentences.i: But I found no one there, not one of God’s creatures.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
